semantics.capability: Capability and AI manifest extension require the exact version and extension hash. ai requires jobs and fire.ai permission; extension is absent from unchanged legacy/non-AI manifests. Only SDK apps may request AI.
semantics.async: request never waits for transport or model output. Use existing jobs.poll/result/cancel/close. One pending AI job per app, within the unchanged four outstanding jobs. All input bytes charge existing callback I/O; no additional frame buffer or timing credit.
semantics.data: data_json is a finite JSON object. App aggregates, samples and labels measurements locally before sending relevant data automatically. No arbitrary files, URLs, tools, credentials or automatic whole-log upload. instructions and data are untrusted app content.
semantics.schema: schema_json is a JSON Schema object for an object result using bounded objects, arrays and string/number/integer/boolean/null values. All object properties required, additionalProperties false; no references, external resources or executable expressions. Apply the JSON limits to both data and results.
semantics.result: Ready job result is {ok=true,data=<bounded parsed JSON object>}; operational failure is {ok=false,error_code=string}. Entire compact UTF-8 result_json is at most result_bytes; reject oversized, invalid, nonfinite or schema-invalid output, never truncate JSON.
semantics.identity: OS supplies app_id, package_id, source_sha256, run_id and boot_id from the actually running verified package. Lua cannot select another identity, model, URL or credentials. Backend authenticates the existing device connection and checks current run/package identity and global/per-app permission.
semantics.lifecycle: Timeout, cancellation, close, app exit, reboot and disconnect prevent completion effects. Backend and device reject stale identity/request results. Cancel does not undo already incurred provider usage. Reconnect requires a fresh request; no automatic charged replay.
semantics.controls: Runtime AI has global and per-app enabled controls and dedicated backend model/configuration. AI Developer AUTO/OFF controls generation of AI-enabled features. AUTO includes AI only for real benefit or an explicit user request. OFF must not silently enable it; explain the conflict. Standard local features remain usable without AI where sensible.
semantics.presentation: Use button-driven actions and clear pending/result/error states. Separate actual observations from AI assessments. Mark offline/fallback content as local; never present fixture or fallback content as real AI output.
semantics.usage: Meter runtime_ai separately from generation/review/dialog, attributed to actual app and request. Report calls, provider tokens, cost confidence and response latency; conservative admission reserves are never displayed as measured spend.

transport.binding: Existing authenticated device WebSocket, existing event envelope and event acknowledgement/dedup; no second server, API key or transport. Runtime event identity must match the actual run. No source comments or app-supplied assertions establish physical execution.
